manual_adversarial_review.scope: Decomposition completeness, dependency ordering, AC mechanicalness, cross-sprint dependencies

findings.description: T1.A and T1.D have circular dependency risk: T1.A creates SKILL.md files with role: fields, T1.D's validator MUST accept those roles. If T1.A's role assignment doesn't pass T1.D's heuristic linter, deployment fails atomically. Mitigation: T1.A's migration script MUST be tested against T1.D's validator BEFORE the atomic commit lands (already covered by T1.A AC #6 'validate-skill-capabilities.sh post-T1.D green against all migrated SKILL.md files' — but the order says 'post-T1.D' which implies T1.D ships first). Recommendation: clarify sequencing — T1.D ships its validator + heuristic linter; T1.A migration is then validated against it before the atomic commit lands. Encode as: T1.A.implement → T1.D.implement → T1.A.commit-atomic. Add note in §3 cross-sprint dependencies section.
findings.action: DEFER to /implement Sprint 1 — engineer/auditor MUST surface this sequencing in their review-sprint findings if T1.A lands before T1.D validator is functional. Not blocking sprint-plan ratification.

findings.description: Sprint 3 operator-action task T3.A.OP requires operator to manually sign cycle-108-baselines-pin git tag. /run sprint-plan executes autonomously — operator-action gates must produce explicit HALT-and-await-operator messaging (not silent stall). SDD §21.3 mentions 'Pre-commit hook verifies signing key matches operator's id' but the autonomous-run flow needs an explicit interrupt point.
findings.action: DEFER to Sprint 3 implementation — /run will halt at T3.A.OP with explicit operator-action message per autonomous run-mode-stop-guard.sh semantics. Not blocking sprint-plan.
